prompts.clone: Clone https://github.com/danielcole-tebra/design-system.git into a separate design-system folder here. If a checkout already exists, inspect and reuse it without overwriting local work. Read AGENTS.md, check Git and Node.js, and tell me the full folder path and any access problems. Keep my new project work outside this repository.
prompts.folders:
My primary folder is for my project work. The separately attached design-system folder contains the shared guidance.

Read its AGENTS.md and use those build and verification rules for this project. Confirm both folder paths. Keep project files and screenshots in my work folder. Run the read-only LIBRARY.md index helper from the design-system checkout. Report missing tools, source-code access and unresolved evidence-recording setup. Do not build in Figma or change repository files yet.
prompts.setup:
Check my Tebra Figma setup before building.
Destination: [paste my new Figma Design file link]
Source library: https://www.figma.com/design/YX2n4YLrEpBXNbcc73T6dw

Read AGENTS.md from the attached design-system folder. Inspect the destination and published library without changing either file. Confirm the exact files, available editing and screenshot tools, and discovery of the components, styles and variables needed for the contact-details exercise in FIRST-RUN.md.

Report font availability, missing access and next steps. Distinguish what you inspected from imports, font loading, editing and screenshot delivery that still need testing during the build. Keep the source library unchanged.
prompts.rebuild:
Read AGENTS.md and FIRST-RUN.md from the attached design-system folder. Follow its build and verification rules. Keep project files and screenshots in my primary work folder.

Starter image: [paste the link to the image in my Figma file]
Destination: [paste my new Figma Design file link]

Inspect the image and rebuild its Edit contact details card in a new, uniquely named “First run · Contact details” section. Preserve the original image and all existing work. Assemble the header, fields, controls and actions as editable library instances and layout frames, using supported properties, bound tokens, library typography and auto layout. Keep published component internals and the source library unchanged.

Build Empty and Filled states, each at 640 and 400 px card widths. Filled uses the image’s fictional values and checked reminder checkbox. Empty clears the fields, contact selection and checkbox. Preserve the title, description, labels and actions; omit the outside-card practice label. State intended action outcomes before assembly. These are static states, not working submission or persistence.

Verify the actual instances, typography, tokens, content and resizing. Report limitations and ask Daniel about unresolved design choices. Capture and inspect the result, display the screenshots in this chat, and link to my editable section. If inline display fails, report it and provide an accessible image link.

Return the “What changed” checklist from FIRST-RUN.md, checking only verified items and listing exceptions separately. Record the batch in the pilot’s agreed evidence repository; report unresolved recording setup. Stop for Daniel’s read before another build batch.

edits.5:14:
You’ll need a local copy of the design-system files. Codex downloads this shared guidance into its own folder; you’ll create a separate folder for your work in step 2.

Choose an easy-to-remember location, such as a folder called Code. Its name and location are up to you. In Codex, start a local chat with access to that location and send this request:

Read AGENTS.md, check Git and Node.js, and tell me the full folder path and any access problems. Keep my new project work outside this repository.
edits.5:18: Codex confirms the saved folder path, such as Code/design-system, and reports missing tools or access. Complete any sign-in or setup it identifies. Keep the path for step 2.
edits.5:26:
1. Create a folder beside design-system for your work. Name it anything, such as Patient intake prototype.

2. In Codex, choose Choose project → New project. Use your work folder as the primary folder.

3. Use Edit project → Add folder to attach the separate design-system folder as a reference.
edits.5:27:
Your work folder holds real project files, notes and screenshots on your computer. Your designs stay in Figma. Later, you can publish your work folder as its own GitHub repository.

Start a chat in your new project and send the prompt below. Use this work-project chat for the remaining Codex steps.
edits.5:30: Codex confirms both folder paths and reads the builder rules. New work goes in your primary folder; the separate clone supplies guidance. Resolve missing tools before continuing.
edits.5:38:
1. Open Settings → Plugins in Codex.

2. Find Figma. Leave it enabled if installed; otherwise install it through Browse directory.

3. Complete any sign-in with your work Figma account. Return to your work-project chat; start a new chat there if the tools have not appeared.
edits.5:39: Ask Codex: “Which Figma tools are available here for inspecting files, editing the canvas, importing library assets and capturing screenshots?”
edits.5:50:
1. Create a Figma Design file in your team’s practice location. Name it Tebra first rebuild · Your name.

2. Create a page named First rebuild.

3. Copy the file link from Share. Keep it for the setup check in step 6.
edits.5:51: This is your destination file. Design System Rebuild is the source library. Sharing your file for feedback is optional; see step 8.
edits.5:47: The new Design file, showing its name, First rebuild page and Share control.
edits.5:62:
1. In your new file, open Assets → Libraries.

2. Find Design System Rebuild. Confirm its source using the link below.

3. Choose Add to file. If it is under Used in this file, it is already added. Close the dialog to browse its assets.
edits.5:63: This manual step is recommended for browsing and editing in Figma. Codex can import accessible published assets without it; library access is still required.
edits.5:74: In your own Codex work-project chat, paste the prompt below. Replace the destination placeholder with the file link from step 4, then send it.

edits.5:95:
1. Open the Figma section Codex links to. Compare the preserved original with the Empty and Filled cards at both widths.

2. Inspect a field or button: it should be an editable library instance. Check spacing, wrapping and content.

3. Review the screenshots and Codex’s checklist. Unverified items stay unchecked, with an explanation.
edits.5:97:
□ Layout containers use auto layout.
□ Fields, dropdown, checkbox and buttons use library instances.
□ Text uses library styles or published typography bindings.
□ Supported colors and spacing are bound to tokens.
□ Both states are checked at 640 and 400 px without clipping.
□ Content and intended actions are preserved or changes explained.
□ The result is editable and the original image is preserved.
□ Screenshots were inspected and shown in chat.

Ask Codex to name any exceptions or unfinished checks.
edits.5:99: The reference uses library floating-label fields and a coral save action. It is an editable form composition built from library controls. Save, Cancel and the dropdown are static; this exercise does not implement their behavior.
edits.5:101:
Tell Codex what needs changing. During the pilot, Daniel’s read is required before the next build batch; wider review ownership is still being settled.

Feedback is optional: post your link to #uxhotline or share it with Daniel Cole. Note where you needed help. Codex keeps the evidence and reports whether the required commit and push succeeded.
